programme: FOXP3 is the lineage-defining transcription factor of regulatory T cells (Tregs); its own target set reproduces the canonical Treg signature (IL2RA/CD25, CTLA4, TNFRSF18/GITR, IKZF2/Helios, GATA3, FASLG). The module is this Treg identity-and-effector circuit — a single factor, but one that alone constitutes a recognizable, textbook programme rather than a loose gene list.
role_in_a: In glioblastoma, FOXP3+ Tregs infiltrate the tumor microenvironment and suppress anti-tumor immunity; blocking FOXP3-intrinsic Treg function sensitizes tumors to chemoradiotherapy (PMID 40582634), and elevated FoxP3+ Treg proportions among tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes track with glioma (PMID 25555571), with gut-microbiome state also modulating intratumoral Foxp3 expression (PMID 35345443).
role_in_b: In ischemic stroke, FOXP3+ Tregs are neuroprotective: pharmacological expansion of this population via a RUNX1/CBFβ/FOXP3 axis reduces post-stroke damage (PMID 41201767), consistent with the broader post-stroke role of Tregs in dampening neuroinflammation and supporting repair.
shared_axis: Both are CNS pathologies in which the size and activity of the local FOXP3+ Treg compartment sets the immune-inflammatory tone of the lesion — the same axis is engaged in each disease, but toward opposite clinical ends: Treg expansion is tumor-permissive in glioblastoma and reparative in ischemic stroke.
reasoning: FOXP3 is placed directly and mechanistically in both diseases by retrieved, disease-specific papers (not reviews or off-topic hits), and the module is nameable from FOXP3's own targets alone without invoking outside knowledge. It is 'supported' rather than 'established' because no retrieved source states a shared GBM-stroke Treg axis as a fact — each disease's Treg involvement is documented separately, and the connection (same factor, opposite valence) is drawn here rather than asserted in the literature.
support: PMID 40582634 — FOXP3 blockade in glioblastoma boosts response to chemoradiotherapy, showing tumor-intrinsic Treg suppression of anti-tumor immunity. PMID 41201767 — a RUNX1/CBFβ/FOXP3 axis drives Treg accumulation and neuroprotection after stroke. PMID 25555571 — increased FoxP3+ Treg proportion among tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in glioblastoma. PMID 35345443 — gut microbiome alterations affect glioma development and Foxp3 expression in the tumor microenvironment.
how_to_falsify: Deplete or block FOXP3+ Tregs (e.g., anti-CD25 depletion or a Treg-specific genetic ablation model) in matched glioblastoma and ischemic-stroke mouse models run under the same protocol. The account predicts opposite effects: Treg depletion should improve anti-tumor control in the glioblastoma model but worsen infarct volume/neuroinflammation in the stroke model. If depletion moves both models in the same direction, or has no effect in either, the shared-axis-with-opposite-valence account fails.
caveats: 24 patient-group comparisons across only 4 independent cohort pairs, blood|brain tissue pairing — a modest replication base for a single-factor claim. FOXP3 itself was concordant in 13/24 comparisons, just over half and well below several other listed factors (e.g. SOX17 at 17/24), so its recurrence, while mechanistically the best-grounded here, is not the strongest signal in the data. The direction of the FOXP3 effect is opposite between the two diseases (harmful in the tumor, protective in ischemia), so this is a shared regulatory axis, not a shared outcome — that asymmetry should not be flattened when interpreting the recurrence counts. NOTCH1 and NFATC1 were excluded as tissue-generic, which rules out a broader generic-immune-TF explanation but does not bear on FOXP3 specifically. None of the other eleven concordant factors (SOX17, ZNF281, TCFL5, ISL1, PRDM16, MEIS1, FOXN1, GTF3A, CREBRF, ZNF354C, NR2F2) had retrieved evidence tying them into this Treg programme, and no attempt is made here to fold them in.
